candidate.title: PRO-cap
candidate.scope: The single PRO-cap route depicted in the assigned Illumina schematic: four-biotin-NTP nuclear run-on, extraction, three streptavidin captures, 3′ adapter introduction, combined Antarctic phosphatase/TAP end repair, 5′ adapter addition, and combined reverse transcription/amplification to cDNA. The collection page heading and caption identify the same PRO-cap target. PRO-seq, GRO-cap and dREG occur in explanatory text or background references and are not additional targets. This is the catalogue schematic implementation, not a claim that every PRO-cap preparation uses identical execution details.

states.label: Amplified cDNA library representing nascent-RNA 5′ ends
features: Readout carrier is amplified cDNA derived from the adapter-flanked RNA.

The catalogue specifies sequencing from the RNA 5′ end. Primary-paper interpretation: these recovered ends locate initiation sites/TSSs of Pol II-engaged nascent RNAs.
This selection-dependent library is not an exhaustive census of all RNA or a demonstrated perfectly specific measure of every initiation event.

operations.label: 4 biotin-labeled NTPs run-on reaction
operations.description: Run-on extends Pol II-engaged nascent RNA with biotin-labeled nucleotides, converting the starting transcript to an affinity-labeled transcript while retaining its capped 5′ end.
operations.mechanism: Incorporation of the first biotin-NTP inhibits further elongation, as reported by the catalogue and the primary PRO-seq chemistry passage. The diagram explicitly supplies four labeled NTPs; the primary paper also discusses single-NTP experiments, which are outside this depicted route.
operations.information_effect: Introduces an affinity handle on nascent RNA synthesized by engaged polymerase during the in vitro run-on; the pre-existing capped 5′ boundary is retained.

evidence.locator: [b00005], shared run-on labeling principle
evidence.quote: Moreover, the incorporation of the first biotin-base inhibits further transcript elongation, ensuring base-pair resolution (fig. S2).
evidence.rationale: This paragraph describes the PRO-seq labeling principle; PRO-cap is identified in [b00009] as a modification using the same Pol II-engaged nascent-RNA pool. The drawing fixes the four-NTP scope here.

operations.label: Extract
operations.description: Extracts the labeled RNA from the polymerase/chromatin context, yielding free biotin-labeled capped RNA.
operations.information_effect: Transfers the nascent-RNA sequence and its cap/biotin features to extracted RNA; no cell identifier or additional molecular index is depicted.

operations.label: Bead coated with streptavidin
operations.description: Captures extracted biotin-labeled RNA on streptavidin-coated beads. The capped RNA changes from free to bead-bound.
operations.mechanism: Streptavidin binds the incorporated biotin handle.
operations.information_effect: Enriches the labeled RNA fraction; binding itself does not identify the RNA start site or prove exclusive biological specificity.

operations.label: Purify

operations.mechanism: Purification and 3′ adapter addition are summarized in this transition. The schematic supplies no separate adapter-ligation caption or internal purification chemistry.
operations.information_effect: Provides the 3′ library interface while retaining the original capped 5′ boundary. No fragmentation is depicted.

operations.label: Antarctic phosphatase and TAP

operations.mechanism: The catalogue calls this 5′ end repair. Differential treatment of capped versus uncapped substrates and exact product end groups are not specified in the supplied main-paper text or schematic.
operations.information_effect: Preserves the RNA sequence boundary formerly marked by the cap while changing its end state for library construction; no discarded-RNA branch is drawn.

corrections.diagram_observation: The diagram labels the workflow PRO-cap, follows a capped nascent RNA through end repair and adapter addition, and ends at cDNA. It depicts no sequencing or pause-mapping panel. The accompanying catalogue description nevertheless ends by saying the 5′-sequenced cDNA maps RNAPII pause sites.
corrections.primary_statement: The supplied full text identifies PRO-cap as detecting initiation sites, and Fig. 2 distinguishes initiation (PRO-cap) from pausing (PRO-seq). The final-state interpretation therefore uses the original RNA 5′ boundary as an initiation/TSS readout while preserving the diagram’s cDNA endpoint.
